title: Brightness controls stop working on a monitor that has been off, asleep, or set to another input during an active session, until the session (or the PowerDevil service) is restarted
line: A DDC/CI monitor that stops answering for a moment, such as when switched to another input, keeps its brightness control instead of losing it until powerdevil restarts.
explanation: When a DDC/CI brightness write still failed after the three retries (1 s, 2 s, 3 s), DDCutilDisplay::ddcBrightnessChangeFinished marked the display as not supporting brightness, and DDCutilPrivateSingleton removed it. It is only added back on a libddcutil connect or DPMS-awake event, which never comes when the monitor is just on another input or slow to answer after resume, so brightness keys, the slider and DDC dimming were gone until powerdevil restarted. Now the failed write is simply given up: the display stays, and the next brightness change (key, slider or dimming) writes again. Real disconnects and sleep are still handled by libddcutil's DISPLAY_DISCONNECTED / DPMS_ASLEEP events.

commits.message:
daemon: Keep DDC/CI displays after a failed brightness write

A monitor that briefly stopped answering DDC/CI, like one set to another
input, was dropped after a failed write until powerdevil restarted. Now
only that write is given up and the next brightness change tries again.

BUG: 528077

From cff360a2c0bee2d8d906c4b63665597f75fbcdd6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 04:28:16 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] daemon: Keep DDC/CI displays after a failed brightness write

A monitor that briefly stopped answering DDC/CI, like one set to another
input, was dropped after a failed write until powerdevil restarted. Now
only that write is given up and the next brightness change tries again.

BUG: 528077
---
 daemon/controllers/ddcutildisplay.cpp | 2 --
 1 file changed, 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/daemon/controllers/ddcutildisplay.cpp b/daemon/controllers/ddcutildisplay.cpp
index 1e0a2f209..eeaf0109f 100644
--- a/daemon/controllers/ddcutildisplay.cpp
+++ b/daemon/controllers/ddcutildisplay.cpp
@@ -225,8 +225,6 @@ void DDCutilDisplay::ddcBrightnessChangeFinished(bool success)
         }
         qCWarning(POWERDEVIL) << "[DDCutilDisplay]:" << m_label << "failed to set DDC/CI brightness";
         m_pendingBrightness.reset();
-        m_supportsBrightness = false;
-        Q_EMIT supportsBrightnessChanged(false);
         return;
     }
 
--

media.caption: Master: brightness key works, monitor 'switched to another input' (fake DDC returns -3007), a key press fails after 3 retries and powerdevil removes the display; after switching back the brightness keys do nothing (no DDC traffic, DisplaysDBusNames empty)
With the fix, same steps: the failed write is given up but the display stays; after switching back the brightness keys write to the monitor again (setvcp 70 OK)
Master journal: 'failed to set DDC/CI brightness', 'Removing display i2c:7', 'No suitable displays detected', then nothing on brightness keys
Fix journal: 'failed to set DDC/CI brightness' without removal; brightness keys after switching back reach the monitor and DisplaysDBusNames still lists display0

review.text: Removing the permanent m_supportsBrightness = false drop on a failed DDC/CI write cleanly fixes the reported root cause, where transient communication failures (such as switching monitor inputs or resuming from sleep) permanently removed brightness controls until powerdevil restarted. Real disconnects remain handled by libddcutil events, and the patch introduces no timer, retry-counter, or lifetime hazards. The before/after logs with the fake DDC/CI harness clearly demonstrate recovery once the monitor responds again, and the separate DimDisplay-stuck-at-30% comments are appropriately left out of scope.

reviews.text: Removing the permanent m_supportsBrightness = false drop on a failed DDC/CI write cleanly fixes the reported root cause, where transient communication failures (such as switching monitor inputs or resuming from sleep) permanently removed brightness controls until powerdevil restarted. Real disconnects remain handled by libddcutil events, and the patch introduces no timer, retry-counter, or lifetime hazards. The before/after logs with the fake DDC/CI harness clearly demonstrate recovery once the monitor responds again, and the separate DimDisplay-stuck-at-30% comments are appropriately left out of scope.

Dropping the 'mark unsupported and remove' step after a failed DDC/CI write is the right fix for the original report (input switched away, or a write just after resume), and the fake-libddcutil rig shows the display staying listed and writable again. But the bug as titled ('off, asleep, or set to another input') and its follow-ups also cover cases this patch does not touch, as the notes admit: c7, c8 and c11 report brightness stuck at 30% dimming after the screen turns off or the system sleeps (also with DDC/CI unchecked, the DimDisplay limit left behind, MR !739), and c6 has libddcutil marking the display ref disconnected (-3020 on open) after the monitors were switched off, so keeping the display without re-opening or re-probing it won't bring control back. A write rejected after a failed undim is also never re-applied once the monitor answers, so it can stay at the wrong level until the next brightness change.
changes: Also fix the stuck-dimming-after-off/sleep variant (DimDisplay's dimming ratio not restored when the action goes away or on wake, the !739 cause) in this series with its own commit, or get the bug split so that symptom is tracked separately (e.g. under 513809) before using BUG: 528077.
Handle the c6 path: when writes fail because libddcutil considers the display ref disconnected/invalid (-3020 etc.), re-open or re-detect the display instead of keeping a dead handle, and test that.

Consider re-applying the last requested brightness/dimming the next time the display answers (or on a successful read), so an undim that failed while the monitor was away doesn't leave it at the wrong level.
